summary.oneLiner: IOLCP delivered record Q4 revenue (INR 619cr, +17.4% YoY) and margin expansion (EBITDA 15.2%, +251bps) driven by near-maximum utilization in chemicals and recovering Ibuprofen demand, while guiding for sustained mid-to-high teen growth in FY27 supported by new Paracetamol capacity ramp-up and a massive INR 1,200-1,400cr greenfield project over 4-5 years.
summary.business: Established in 1986, IOL operates through two primary business segments: Pharmaceuticals and Specialty Chemicals. The pharmaceutical business develops and manufactures a diversified portfolio of APIs spanning multiple therapeutic categories used in essential medicines, while the specialty chemicals business (established 1996) manufactures products such as Ethyl Acetate, Acetic Anhydride and Triacetin for a wide range of industrial applications, serving both captive requirements and merchant sales. Manufacturing is fully backward integrated, which the company says strengthens efficiency, product quality, supply reliability and cost competitiveness across regulated and semi-regulated markets.

currentContext.expansion: IOL operates from a single, fully integrated manufacturing complex at Barnala, Punjab, spanning 180+ acres, bringing API and specialty chemical production together at one location with shared utilities and comprehensive backward integration. The complex comprises 18 manufacturing units across the API and chemical divisions with a stated total installed capacity of 2,13,126 MTPA, including dedicated and multi-product facilities, regulatory-approved production blocks (USFDA-audited and EUGMP-approved units) and highly automated, DCS-based chemical plants. During FY 2025-26 the Company continued to invest in capacity expansion, automation and process optimisation, with ALL capital expenditure funded through internal accruals. Named expansion actions during the year: Ethyl Acetate capacity was enhanced from 1,00,000 MTPA to 1,20,000 MTPA at a capital expenditure of approximately Rs 4 crore; Acetic Anhydride capacity was increased from 25,000 MTPA to 32,000 MTPA at a capital expenditure of approximately Rs 5.71 crore; and Triacetin capacity (6,000 MTPA) was commissioned. On the pharmaceutical side, Unit 11, the dedicated fully backward-integrated Paracetamol facility of 10,800 MTPA, was commissioned and scaled, expanding manufacturing scale in the analgesics segment. Minoxidil was commercially launched during the year (Unit 9B, 120 MTP installed) and nine additional molecules remain under development. Backward integration extends to key starting materials, including in-house Iso Butyl Benzene (12,000 MTPA) for the Ibuprofen chain. An environmental impact assessment was undertaken for the 'Expansion of Chemicals and APIs production unit at Village & Post Fatehgarh Channa, Mansa Road, District Barnala', conducted by an independent external agency with results communicated in the public domain. Regulatory milestones supporting the expanded platform include a Certificate of GMP Compliance of Manufacturer from the National Institute of Pharmacy and Nutrition, Hungary, and EDQM Certificates of Suitability for Pantoprazole Sodium Sesquihydrate Process-III, Metformin Hydrochloride Process-II, Sitagliptin Phosphate Monohydrate, Minoxidil and Clopidogrel Besilate. risks.note: Named by management as a risk category: 'Dependence on a limited number of products and therapeutic segments', with stated impact of 'exposure to market volatility, pricing pressure and fluctuations in demand affecting profitability'. Structurally relevant because the Company is among the world's largest Ibuprofen manufacturers and Ibuprofen alone contributes 34.43% of total turnover (BRSR LCA table), with Ethyl Acetate a further 33.66% — i.e. two molecules account for roughly two-thirds of revenue. Mitigation stated: portfolio diversification across APIs and specialty chemicals, supported by expansion into new products and markets (non-Ibuprofen APIs up from 18% in FY21 to 37% in FY26).

risks.risk: Single-site / single-complex operational concentration and fire & industrial hazard exposure
risks.note: All manufacturing is at one fully integrated complex at Barnala, Punjab (BRSR: 1 plant nationally, no international plants). Management flags 'Fire and Industrial Hazards' arising from fire incidents, equipment malfunction, unsafe conditions or process failures, with impact of damage to assets and infrastructure, production disruptions, financial losses and employee safety incidents. Any event at the single site would affect both the API and chemical divisions simultaneously. Mitigation: fire protection systems, periodic safety drills, awareness programmes, emergency response procedures, robust EHS systems, periodic audits and environmental monitoring.

risks.risk: Occupational health & safety, including a fatality recorded in the year
risks.note: Occupational Health & Safety, Emergency Preparedness and Safe Material Handling are all classified as Social RISK material topics, and the BRSR materiality table notes Health & Safety can 'directly impact people and community and disrupt the operations' with NEGATIVE financial implications. Materially, the BRSR safety table discloses 1 employee fatality and 1 total recordable work-related injury in FY 2025-26 against nil in FY 2024-25, with employee LTIFR rising from 0 to 1.46 per million person-hours — against a stated target of Zero Lost Time Fatality Rate. Mitigation: ISO 45001:2018-certified OHS management system covering 100% of plants and offices, HIRA/JSA/HAZOP/AIA/PSSR methodologies, an online Incident Prevention Opportunity (IPO) hazard-reporting portal, EHS training and periodic mock drills.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and raw-material dependence
risks.note: Root causes stated: dependence on key suppliers, logistics bottlenecks, geopolitical developments, natural disasters and equipment failures; impact stated as production interruptions, delayed deliveries, increased costs and revenue loss. Mitigation: supplier diversification, strategic inventory management, business continuity planning, cross-functional response mechanisms, and — structurally — backward integration across key intermediates including in-house Iso Butyl Benzene.

risks.risk: Product quality variability and regulatory/compliance exposure
risks.note: Classified as a Regulatory & Compliance risk. Root causes: process deviations, raw material inconsistencies, equipment issues and non-conformance to quality standards; impact: customer complaints, product recalls, regulatory action, revenue loss and reputational impact. Structurally acute because the Company supplies regulated markets under USFDA DMFs and EDQM CEPs from USFDA-audited and EUGMP-approved units, so a quality failure has market-access consequences. Product Quality is also flagged as a Governance RISK material topic. Mitigation: robust quality management systems, regular audits, process controls, employee training and continuous improvement, supported by TrackWise, LIMS and SAP.

risks.risk: Environmental compliance — effluent, emissions and hazardous waste
risks.note: Air Emissions, GHG Emissions, Hazardous Waste Management and Waste Water Treatment are all classified as Environmental RISK material topics. The BRSR materiality table identifies 'effluent generation from process having potential of water pollution and soil pollution' as the lead issue, and the LCA risk table adds 'social risks involve health and safety impacts on employees and local communities'. Structurally relevant because operations are chemistry-intensive and concentrated at one site. Mitigation: 100% Zero Liquid Discharge process treating, recycling and reusing water; ISO 14001:2015 audited by BSI; biofuel use in the captive power plant; Continuous Air Quality Monitoring System (CAQMS); authorised disposal and recycling channels. Note that BRSR discloses total waste generated rising to 8,693.23 MT in FY26 from 4,394.98 MT in FY25, with 'other hazardous waste' at 6,670.12 MT vs 2,705.21 MT, and Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions both rising, alongside the production expansion.

Named as the Financial risk category: 'Fluctuations in exchange rates impacting imports and export realisations', with impact of margin pressure, cost escalation and volatility in earnings. Structurally relevant given exports are 24% of total turnover across 70 international countries. Mitigation: continuous monitoring of currency exposure, hedging strategies and periodic market reviews.

risks.risk: Cyber attack / information security and data privacy
risks.note: Named as an Operational risk driven by increasing digitalisation, evolving cyber threats and unauthorised access attempts, with impact spanning operational disruptions, data breaches, regulatory non-compliance, financial losses and reputational damage; Data Privacy, Information Security and Counterfeit Risk are separately classified as Governance RISK material topics. Mitigation: comprehensive cybersecurity and IT governance frameworks, regular Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT), continuous monitoring and preventive controls; the Company is certified to ISO 27001.

risks.risk: Innovation / R&D under-investment and business continuity
risks.note: Innovation and R&D Risk is flagged: insufficient investment in R&D, technology and talent development would lead to reduced product innovation, slower new product development and loss of competitive advantage — material given nine molecules are in development and the diversification strategy depends on new commercialisations. Business Continuity Disruption is separately flagged (unforeseen events affecting critical operations, leading to operational interruptions, delayed deliveries, revenue loss and stakeholder dissatisfaction), mitigated by an established Business Continuity Plan, defined recovery protocols and periodic Business Impact Analysis reviews. Ethical Conduct & Monitoring is a further named risk, mitigated by internal controls, whistle-blower mechanisms and periodic compliance reviews.

one-line thesis: IOLCP delivered record Q4 revenue (INR 619cr, +17.4% YoY) and margin expansion (EBITDA 15.2%, +251bps) driven by near-maximum utilization in chemicals and recovering Ibuprofen demand, while guiding for sustained mid-to-high teen growth in FY27 supported by new Paracetamol capacity ramp-up and a massive INR 1,200-1,400cr greenfield project over 4-5 years.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Established in 1986, IOL operates through two primary business segments: Pharmaceuticals and Specialty Chemicals. The pharmaceutical business develops and manufactures a diversified portfolio of APIs spanning multiple therapeutic categories used in essential medicines, while the specialty chemicals business (established 1996) manufactures products such as Ethyl Acetate, Acetic Anhydride and Triacetin for a wide range of industrial applications, serving both captive requirements and merchant sales. Manufacturing is fully backward integrated, which the company says strengthens efficiency, product quality, supply reliability and cost competitiveness across regulated and semi-regulated markets.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Long-term outlook for both pharmaceutical and specialty chemical industries described as encouraging, supported by increasing healthcare demand, expanding global manufacturing opportunities and India's strengthening role as supply chains diversify
- Specialty chemicals industry began showing signs of recovery following an extended period of inventory correction; management believes its integrated platform positions it to capitalise as global specialty chemical demand gradually recovers
- Healthy demand seen during FY26 in Paracetamol, Metformin, Pantoprazole, Clopidogrel, Fenofibrate and Levetiracetam, increasing the contribution of non-Ibuprofen products
- Scaling of the fully integrated Paracetamol facility (commissioned in the previous year) strengthened manufacturing capability, supply reliability and operational efficiencies
- Backward integration benefits — improved supply assurance, enhanced cost efficiencies and greater operational efficiency/resilience — described as increasingly evident during the year
- Headwinds acknowledged for FY26: geopolitical uncertainty, pricing pressure and evolving market dynamics
- Macro backdrop cited: global economy grew ~3.5% in CY2025 (advanced 1.9%, EMDEs 4.5%); IMF projects global GDP growth of 3.0% in CY2026 and 3.4% in CY2027
- Indian economy grew 7.6% in FY 2025-26 with PFCE +7.7% and GFCF +7.1%; repo rate cut by 100 bps to 5.25%; capacity utilisation improved to approximately 75-76%
- Union Budget 2026-27 public capex of approximately Rs 12.2 lakh crore (3.1% of GDP) and continued emphasis on manufacturing, infrastructure and export competitiveness expected to create a favourable operating environment for pharmaceutical and specialty chemical manufacturers such as IOL
- India-EU FTA cited as a positive — preferential market access for over 99% of Indian exports, expected to benefit Indian pharmaceutical exporters through improved market access and reduced trade barriers
- Global pharmaceutical sales estimated at approximately $1.7-1.8 trillion in CY2025 with industry growth of 6-7%; projected to reach approximately $1.8-1.9 trillion in CY2026
- Global generic formulations market projected to grow at a CAGR of 5-6.5% to US$570-720 billion by the early 2030s, supported by patent expiries, affordability demand, chronic disease burden and biosimilar adoption
- Indian pharmaceutical industry valued at approximately US$65 billion in FY 2025-26, projected to reach US$130 billion by 2030 and approximately US$450 billion by 2047; India's share of the global pharmaceutical market projected to rise from ~3-3.5% to nearly 5% by 2030
- Indian pharma exports exceeded USD 30 billion in FY 2025-26, up 5.6% YoY, to over 200 countries
- Sector risks flagged in the industry narrative: pricing pressure in regulated markets, rising compliance costs, loss of exclusivity for key products, outcome-based pricing models, and intensifying generic/biosimilar competition
- Growth drivers named for Indian pharma: ageing population approaching 230 million by 2036, rising disposable income, increasing chronic disease burden, digitalisation of healthcare, and health insurance projected to grow at ~15% CAGR over the next five years (the 'Favourable Government' driver row is cut off mid-heading in the routed text)

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: IOL operates from a single, fully integrated manufacturing complex at Barnala, Punjab, spanning 180+ acres, bringing API and specialty chemical production together at one location with shared utilities and comprehensive backward integration. The complex comprises 18 manufacturing units across the API and chemical divisions with a stated total installed capacity of 2,13,126 MTPA, including dedicated and multi-product facilities, regulatory-approved production blocks (USFDA-audited and EUGMP-approved units) and highly automated, DCS-based chemical plants. During FY 2025-26 the Company continued to invest in capacity expansion, automation and process optimisation, with ALL capital expenditure funded through internal accruals. Named expansion actions during the year: Ethyl Acetate capacity was enhanced from 1,00,000 MTPA to 1,20,000 MTPA at a capital expenditure of approximately Rs 4 crore; Acetic Anhydride capacity was increased from 25,000 MTPA to 32,000 MTPA at a capital expenditure of approximately Rs 5.71 crore; and Triacetin capacity (6,000 MTPA) was commissioned. On the pharmaceutical side, Unit 11, the dedicated fully backward-integrated Paracetamol facility of 10,800 MTPA, was commissioned and scaled, expanding manufacturing scale in the analgesics segment. Minoxidil was commercially launched during the year (Unit 9B, 120 MTP installed) and nine additional molecules remain under development. Backward integration extends to key starting materials, including in-house Iso Butyl Benzene (12,000 MTPA) for the Ibuprofen chain. An environmental impact assessment was undertaken for the 'Expansion of Chemicals and APIs production unit at Village & Post Fatehgarh Channa, Mansa Road, District Barnala', conducted by an independent external agency with results communicated in the public domain. Regulatory milestones supporting the expanded platform include a Certificate of GMP Compliance of Manufacturer from the National Institute of Pharmacy and Nutrition, Hungary, and EDQM Certificates of Suitability for Pantoprazole Sodium Sesquihydrate Process-III, Metformin Hydrochloride Process-II, Sitagliptin Phosphate Monohydrate, Minoxidil and Clopidogrel Besilate. NOTE ON TRUNCATION: the routed MD&A 'Specialty Chemicals Portfolio' paragraph breaks off mid-word ('broadens our reve'), and the routed BRSR extract ends mid-word ('Environ') in the environmental-impact-assessment table, so the closing detail of both is not available.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Fully backward integrated manufacturing platform — in-house production of key intermediates retains value in the business and supports a structural cost advantage, supply assurance and cost efficiencies
- Among the world's largest and most integrated manufacturers of Ibuprofen; significant presence in Metformin and Ethyl Acetate
- Regulatory reach: 14 USFDA DMFs and 21 EDQM CEPs supporting presence across regulated markets including Brazil, Korea, Taiwan and Russia
- Product-mix diversification — contribution of non-Ibuprofen APIs increased from 18% in FY21 to 37% in FY26, driven by Paracetamol, Clopidogrel and Pantoprazole
- DSIR-approved R&D centre with over 120 professionals including more than 50 scientists, focused on green chemistry, process innovation, cost-efficient synthesis and backward integration
- Balance-sheet flexibility — described as a 'near debt free balance sheet with a debt equity ratio of 0.08', with planned capital expenditure funded primarily through internal accruals
- Credit rating reaffirmed by CARE Ratings: 'CARE A+' (Outlook: Stable) for long-term bank facilities and 'CARE A1+' for short-term bank facilities
- Land bank for future growth — 101 acres acquired during the year with environmental clearances, creating a foundation for the next phase of capacity expansion
- Sustainability credentials used as a commercial differentiator — 100% ZLD, 100% water neutrality, EcoVadis Gold, ~80% of power requirements from renewable sources
- Workforce of over 3,000 employees (BRSR: 3,095 permanent employees, 3,592 total)
